title: Bake the light maps
author: claude
summary: Blender works out the light on each surface and saves one picture per group of surfaces.
what: Blender works out the light on each surface and saves one picture per group of surfaces: the floor, each wall, the ceiling, the rug, the credenza and more.
why: These pictures are the baked light. The web page lays them over the room.
how:
- The bake keeps the direct and the bounced light, but no colour.
- Each light map sits on a second set of coordinates on the surface.
- Bigger surfaces get bigger pictures: 2048 pixels for the floor, each wall, the ceiling, the rug and the credenza; 1024 for the curtains, art, terrace, plants and fig; 512 for the window and lamp.
- The rug uses a flat top-down mapping.

tech.plain: Blender's realistic renderer. It follows light the way a camera would see it.
